business_model.claim: Suburban Propane Partners, L.P. distributes propane, renewable propane, renewable natural gas, fuel oil, and refined fuels, markets natural gas and electricity in deregulated markets, produces and invests in low-carbon fuel alternatives, and installs and services home comfort equipment.
quotes: We specialize in the distribution of propane, renewable propane, renewable natural gas (“RNG”), fuel oil and refined fuels, as well as the marketing of natural gas and electricity in deregulated markets and production of and investing in low-carbon fuel alternatives.
In support of our core marketing and distribution operations, we install and service a variety of home comfort equipment, particularly in the areas of heating and ventilation.

business_model.claim: The Partnership serves approximately 1.0 million residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural customers through approximately 750 locations across 42 states, concentrated on the east and west coasts, portions of the midwest, and Alaska.
quotes: As of September 27, 2025, we were serving the energy needs of approximately 1.0 million residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural customers through approximately 750 locations in 42 states with operations principally concentrated in the east and west coast regions of the United States, as well as portions of the midwest region of the United States and Alaska.

business_model.claim: Approximately 93% of propane gallons sold went to retail customers—43% residential, 39% commercial, 8% industrial, 6% government, and 4% agricultural—with approximately 7% for risk management activities and wholesale customers, and no single customer accounted for 10% or more of propane revenues.
quotes: Approximately 93% of our propane gallons sold in fiscal 2025 were to retail customers: 43% of those propane gallons to residential customers, 39% to commercial customers, 8% to industrial customers, 6% to government customers and 4% to agricultural customers.
The balance of approximately 7% of our propane gallons sold in fiscal 2025 were for risk management activities and wholesale customers.
No single customer accounted for 10% or more of our propane revenues during fiscal 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (tank ownership comparison stated in P2)
business_model.claim: The Partnership delivers retail propane via bobtail trucks into stationary customer-site storage tanks (a significant portion owned by the Partnership) and portable cylinders, delivers to bulk end users via transport trucks, supplies approximately 60% of residential customers through an automatic delivery system, and offers a budget payment plan.
quotes: Retail deliveries of propane are usually made to customers by means of bobtail and rack trucks.
As is common in the propane industry, we own a significant portion of the storage tanks located on our customers’ premises.
Approximately 60% of our residential customers receive their propane supply through an automatic delivery system.

business_model.claim: Under its prior reporting structure, the Partnership reported Propane, Fuel Oil and Refined Fuels, and Natural Gas and Electricity alongside All Other, generating total revenues of $1,432,518 (table in thousands): Propane $1,265,494, Fuel oil and refined fuels 67,352, Natural gas and electricity 24,593, and All other 75,079.
quotes: As described below, we manage and evaluate our operations in four operating segments, three of which are reportable segments: Propane, Fuel Oil and Refined Fuels and Natural Gas and Electricity.

business_model.claim: Prior to the segment realignment, Total Revenues were $ 1,182,971 (table in thousands), consisting of Propane $ 1,044,492, Fuel Oil and Refined Fuels 62,244, Natural Gas and Electricity 19,199, and All Other $ 57,036.

The Partnership modified the composition of its operating and reportable segments to Propane (distribution of propane, renewable propane, other fuels and related services) and Renewable Natural Gas (production and injection of RNG).
quotes: As of September 26, 2026, the Partnership modified the composition of its operating and reportable segments to provide greater transparency into the operating and financial performance of its businesses and better align its financial reporting with how management evaluates performance and allocates resources.
As a result, the Partnership’s two reportable segments are Propane and Renewable Natural Gas.
The Propane segment includes activities associated with the distribution of propane, renewable propane, other fuels and related services.
The Renewable Natural Gas segment includes activities associated with the production and injection of RNG.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P4, and P8 (risks stated in P2 and P3)
business_model.claim: Through Suburban Renewable Energy, the Partnership produces and injects RNG at Stanfield, Arizona, receives tipping fees for processing food waste into fertilizer and biogas in Columbus, Ohio (with gas upgrading equipment installed awaiting commissioning), placed a new anaerobic digester facility in Upstate New York into service, and holds minority investments in Independence Hydrogen and Oberon Fuels.
quotes: The RNG platform includes the following: (1) a large-scale RNG production facility in Stanfield, Arizona that is currently operating and includes seven anaerobic digesters, manure rights from approximately 55,000 dairy cattle and an interconnect with an interstate pipeline and (2) an operating facility in Columbus, Ohio that is currently receiving tipping fees from several large food and beverage providers for processing food waste into fertilizer and biogas, and has an active development project to upgrade the biogas into RNG for sale.

Combined with the contribution from our new anaerobic digester facility in Upstate New York, which was placed into service in July, average daily RNG injection for fiscal 2026 increased 13% compared to the prior year.

We also completed the installation of gas upgrading equipment at our existing anaerobic digestion facility in Columbus, Ohio, and we are awaiting final commissioning of the injection site by the local utility.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P5, and P8
business_model.claim: RNG production and renewable propane sales generate environmental attributes and tax credits; the Partnership recognized $12.4 million of production tax credit benefits and generated $11.3 million of investment tax credits, monetizing approximately $3.0 million of the production tax credits.
quotes: During fiscal 2026, we recognized $12.4 million of benefits from production tax credits (“PTCs”) related to RNG injections for the period from January 2025 through September 2026 and generated $11.3 million of investment tax credits (“ITCs”) associated with qualifying expenditures for the construction of our facility in Upstate New York.
We monetized approximately $3.0 million of the PTCs during fiscal 2026 and expect to monetize the remaining PTCs and the ITCs during fiscal 2027.

business_model.claim: Demand and sales volumes are seasonal, with approximately two-thirds of retail propane volume and approximately three-fourths of retail fuel oil volume typically sold during the October through March peak heating season.
quotes: The volume of propane, fuel oil and natural gas sold is at its highest during the six-month peak heating season of October through March and is directly affected by the severity and length of the winter months.
Typically, we sell approximately two-thirds of our retail propane volume and approximately three-fourths of our retail fuel oil volume during the peak heating season.

business_model.claim: Warmer-than-normal temperatures curb heating demand while regional cold snaps lift volumes; retail propane sales reached 402.9 million gallons (up approximately 1%) as average temperatures were 8% warmer than normal and 1% cooler than the prior year.
quotes: Retail propane gallons sold in fiscal 2026 of 402.9 million gallons increased approximately 1% compared to the prior year.
Average temperatures (as measured by heating degree days) across all of the Partnership’s service territories for fiscal 2026 were 8% warmer than normal and 1% cooler than the prior year.

business_model.claim: Retail selling prices fluctuate with wholesale commodity costs (such as Mont Belvieu and Conway postings), driving revenue changes alongside volume, while high prices can trigger customer conservation and competition from natural gas pipelines, electricity, and local distributors.
quotes: Therefore, average retail sales prices can vary significantly from year to year as our costs fluctuate with the propane, fuel oil, crude oil and natural gas commodity markets and infrastructure conditions.
High prices can lead to customer conservation, resulting in reduced demand for our products.
The retail propane and fuel oil industries are mature and highly competitive.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P8
business_model.claim: The Partnership expands its customer base and counter-seasonal verticals through selective acquisitions, including a New Mexico and Arizona propane business for approximately $53.0 million, California businesses for $24.0 million, and a Florida business for $6.2 million.
quotes: We supplement our organic customer base growth and retention initiatives with selective acquisitions of high-quality propane businesses in strategic markets, as well as identifying and fostering new market expansion efforts to establish or extend our presence and expand market share.

We also continued to invest in our propane platform, acquiring two well-run businesses in strategic markets in California for $24.0 million and, subsequent to the end of the fiscal year, a high-quality business in Florida for $6.2 million.

business_model.claim: Profitability depends largely on the spread between retail selling prices and product acquisition and transportation costs; Cost of products sold was $563,706 (table in thousands) and represented 39.4% of total revenues.
quotes: The level of profitability in the retail propane, fuel oil, natural gas and electricity businesses is largely dependent on the difference between retail sales price and our costs to acquire and transport products.

The cost of products sold reported in the consolidated statements of operations represents the weighted average unit cost of propane, fuel oil and refined fuels, and natural gas and electricity sold, including transportation costs to deliver product from our supply points to storage or to our customer service centers.
Cost of products sold also includes the cost of appliances and related parts sold or installed by our customer service centers computed on a basis that approximates the average cost of the products.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: Propane supply is purchased from approximately 45 wholesalers at approximately 140 supply points under agreements typically indexed to hubs such as Mont Belvieu, Texas and Conway, Kansas, supplemented by spot purchases, forward fixed-price contracts, and NYMEX/third-party derivatives.
quotes: Our propane supply is purchased from approximately 45 wholesalers at approximately 140 supply points located throughout the United States and Canada.

Our propane supply contracts typically provide for pricing based upon index formulas using the posted prices established at major supply points such as Mont Belvieu, Texas, or Conway, Kansas (plus transportation costs) at the time of delivery.

We enter into propane forward, options and swap agreements with third parties, and use futures and options contracts traded on the New York Mercantile Exchange (“NYMEX”) to purchase and sell propane, fuel oil, crude oil, natural gas and electricity at fixed prices in the future.

business_model.claim: Combined operating and general and administrative expenses reached $603.1 million (an increase of $22.8 million, or 3.9%), driven by payroll and benefit-related expenses, fuel and vehicle maintenance costs, and self-insurance claim accruals, partially offset by an RNG acquisition insurance recovery.
quotes: Combined operating and general and administrative expenses of $603.1 million for fiscal 2026 increased $22.8 million, or 3.9%, compared to the prior year.

The increase was primarily attributable to higher payroll and benefit-related expenses, increased fuel and vehicle maintenance costs, and higher accruals for self-insurance claims, offset to an extent by an insurance recovery related to the partial settlement of certain claims associated with the Partnership’s acquisition of RNG production assets in December 2022.

business_model.claim: Inflationary pressures, competition for supply-chain resources, tariffs, and trade conflicts increase labor, transportation, operating, tank, equipment, and capital expansion costs, alongside expenses for a multi-year technology modernization initiative.
quotes: Although we have not experienced significant disruptions with securing the products we sell, inflationary factors and competition for resources across the supply chain have resulted in increased costs in a wide variety of areas, including labor, transportation costs, operating costs and the cost of capital expansion projects, tanks and other equipment.

These and other factors, including the impact of tariffs and trade conflicts, may continue to impact our product costs, expenses, and capital expenditures, and could continue to have an impact on consumer demand as consumers manage the impact of inflation and tariffs on their resources.

In fiscal 2025, we embarked on a multi-year technology modernization initiative intended to simplify the way we operate, consolidate our systems platform and improve the tools we use to serve our customers and employees.

business_model.basis: stated in F1, F2, and P1
business_model.claim: The Partnership carries 1,223,910 (table in thousands) in long-term borrowings, incurred 58,298 (table in thousands) of net interest expense and 49,788 (table in thousands) of depreciation and amortization, and pays corporate-level income taxes on its Corporate Entities subsidiaries.
quotes: Long-term borrowings | 1,223,910 | 1,211,745

Our fuel oil and refined fuels, natural gas and electricity, services and renewable energy businesses are structured as either limited liability companies that are treated as corporations or corporate entities (collectively referred to as “Corporate Entities”) and, as such, are subject to corporate level income tax.

business_model.basis: stated in F3, P4, and P7
business_model.claim: Investments in unconsolidated affiliates have generated equity in losses and impairment charges totaling 1,437 (table in thousands) versus 23,372 (table in thousands) in the prior-year period, including full impairments of Oberon Fuels and another development-stage entity and a write-down of Independence Hydrogen.
quotes: Equity in losses and impairment charges for investments in unconsolidated affiliates | 1,437 | 23,372

Due to Oberon’s financial condition, which raised substantial doubts about its ability to continue as a going concern, as well as the uncertainty about potential third-party capital infusion, the Partnership determined that its investment in Oberon was fully impaired as of December 28, 2024.

competitive_position.claim: Suburban Propane believes it is the third-largest retail marketer of propane in the United States based on calendar year 2024 retail gallons sold.
quotes: We believe, based on LP/Gas Magazine dated February 2025, that we are the third-largest retail marketer of propane in the United States, measured by retail gallons sold in calendar year 2024.

competitive_position.claim: The partnership has operated in retail propane since 1928 and serves approximately 1.0 million customers through approximately 750 locations in 42 states.
quotes: Together with our predecessor companies, we have been continuously engaged in the retail propane business since 1928.

As of September 27, 2025, we were serving the energy needs of approximately 1.0 million residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural customers through approximately 750 locations in 42 states with operations principally concentrated in the east and west coast regions of the United States, as well as portions of the midwest region of the United States and Alaska.

competitive_position.claim: Retail propane sales totaled 400.5 million gallons in fiscal 2025 and 402.9 million gallons in fiscal 2026, an increase of approximately 1%.
quotes: Retail propane gallons sold in fiscal 2025 totaled 400.5 million gallons, an increase of 5.9% compared to the prior year.
Retail propane gallons sold in fiscal 2026 of 402.9 million gallons increased approximately 1% compared to the prior year.

competitive_position.claim: Suburban Propane owns a significant portion of the stationary storage tanks on propane customers' premises and delivers automatically to approximately 60% of residential customers.
quotes: Approximately 60% of our residential customers receive their propane supply through an automatic delivery system.
As is common in the propane industry, we own a significant portion of the storage tanks located on our customers’ premises.

competitive_position.claim: Customer service centers are typically located in suburban and rural areas lacking natural gas, and no single customer accounted for 10% or more of fiscal 2025 propane revenues.
quotes: Typically, our customer service centers are located in suburban and rural areas where natural gas is not readily available.
No single customer accounted for 10% or more of our propane revenues during fiscal 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1 for supplier and point counts; pricing pass-through limitation stated in P2 and P3
competitive_position.claim: The partnership sources propane from approximately 45 wholesalers across approximately 140 supply points in the United States and Canada.
quotes: Our propane supply is purchased from approximately 45 wholesalers at approximately 140 supply points located throughout the United States and Canada.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) and P8 (FY2026 earnings release)
competitive_position.claim: Adjusted EBITDA rose 2.2% to $284.0 million in fiscal 2026 after rising 11.2% to $278.0 million in fiscal 2025, aided by propane unit margin increases of $0.05 per gallon in fiscal 2026.
quotes: Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (“Adjusted EBITDA,” as defined and reconciled below) increased $28.0 million, or 11.2%, to $278.0 million for fiscal 2025, compared to $250.0 million in the prior year.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (“Adjusted EBITDA,” as defined and reconciled below) increased $6.0 million, or 2.2%, to $284.0 million for fiscal 2026, compared to $278.0 million in the prior year.

Excluding the impact of these unrealized mark-to-market adjustments, gross margin for fiscal 2026 increased $32.7 million, or 3.8%, compared to the prior year, primarily due to an increase in propane unit margins of $0.05 per gallon, or 2.5%, higher propane volumes sold, and the benefit of $12.4 million from PTCs recognized during fiscal 2026 on RNG injections.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) and P8 (FY2026 earnings release)
competitive_position.claim: The partnership expanded through propane acquisitions of $53.0 million in New Mexico and Arizona, $24.0 million in California, and $6.2 million in Florida, while average daily RNG injection increased 13% in fiscal 2026.
quotes: We acquired and integrated a well-run propane business in strategic markets in New Mexico and Arizona for total consideration of approximately $53.0 million;

We also continued to invest in our propane platform, acquiring two well-run businesses in strategic markets in California for $24.0 million and, subsequent to the end of the fiscal year, a high-quality business in Florida for $6.2 million.

Combined with the contribution from our new anaerobic digester facility in Upstate New York, which was placed into service in July, average daily RNG injection for fiscal 2026 increased 13% compared to the prior year.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: The retail propane and fuel oil industries are mature and highly fragmented, with overall demand expected to remain flat to moderately declining over the next several years.
quotes: The retail propane and fuel oil industries are mature and highly competitive.
We expect overall demand for propane and fuel oil to be relatively flat to moderately declining over the next several years.

Competition in the retail propane business is highly fragmented and generally occurs on a local basis with other large full-service multi-state propane marketers, thousands of smaller local independent marketers and farm cooperatives.

competitive_position.claim: Fuel oil customers generally own their own tanks, intensifying competition, while natural gas and electricity segment revenues fell 5.0% to $24.6 million in fiscal 2025 due to a lower customer base.
quotes: In addition, our existing fuel oil customers, unlike our existing propane customers, generally own their own tanks, which can result in intensified competition for these customers.

Revenues in our natural gas and electricity segment decreased $1.3 million, or 5.0%, to $24.6 million in fiscal 2025 compared to $25.9 million in the prior year, resulting from lower electricity sales, primarily due to the impact of a lower customer base.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Propane and fuel oil face competition from electricity and natural gas, with natural gas currently significantly less expensive per equivalent BTU where pipelines exist.
quotes: Propane and fuel oil compete with electricity, natural gas and other existing and future sources of energy, some of which are, or may in the future be, less costly for equivalent energy value.
For example, natural gas currently is a significantly less expensive source of energy than propane and fuel oil on an equivalent BTU basis.
The gradual expansion of the nation’s natural gas distribution systems has made natural gas available in areas that previously depended upon propane or fuel oil.

competitive_position.claim: Heating demand is highly vulnerable to warm weather, with service-territory temperatures running 8% warmer than normal in fiscal 2026 and 9%, 13%, and 8% warmer than normal in fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023.
quotes: For example, average temperatures in our service territories were 9% warmer than normal for fiscal 2025, 13% warmer than normal for fiscal 2024 and 8% warmer than normal for fiscal 2023, as measured by the number of heating degree days reported by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
Average temperatures (as measured by heating degree days) across all of the Partnership’s service territories for fiscal 2026 were 8% warmer than normal and 1% cooler than the prior year.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Policies promoting electrification and restricting fossil fuels threaten core fuel sales, while RNG economics depend on volatile RIN and LCFS credit markets, federal tax credits, and third-party pipelines.
quotes: While our emerging renewable energy platform may benefit from additional incentives for the growth of renewable energy, our sale of propane, fuel oil and refined fuels, and natural gas may experience significant negative impact from the restrictions placed on the use of fossil fuels.
Additionally, the markets where RINs and LCFS Credits are traded, have experienced volatility over past years and may experience continued volatility in the future.
We also anticipate that the renewable energy market will be increasingly competitive, which could impact our ability to meet our long-term strategic growth initiatives.

competitive_position.claim: Volatile wholesale fuel costs, inflation, and tariffs can squeeze margins if cost increases cannot be passed through promptly, while high retail prices drive customer conservation.
quotes: Because we may not be able to pass on to our customers immediately, or in full, all increases in our wholesale and transportation costs of our products, these increases could reduce our profitability.
High prices can lead to customer conservation, resulting in reduced demand for our products.

quotes: There is no assurance that we will be able to pass on product acquisition and transportation cost increases fully or immediately, particularly when such costs increase rapidly.
High prices can lead to customer conservation, resulting in reduced demand for our products.
